positions.title: Student Programmer
positions.description:
As a work-study college, Berea students are expected to work at least 10 hours a week on some function of the college. As a student programmer, my goal is to create and maintain software applications for the campus students and faculty to use.

In this position, I have learned the fundamentals of software engineering and gained an understanding of the software development cycle. Using Flask, HTML, JavaScript, Rails, and other technologies I have developed or helped develop and maintained four different systems used by the college (BART, URCPP, CAS, BCSR). 

I have gained excellent communication and interpersonal skills by working and collaborating with a growing team of students. Achievements for this position include a labor award for my efforts in this position and a promotion to lead programmer charged with leading a coaching new student programmers.

positions.title: PHETsimulations Contributor
positions.description:
– Used object-oriented programming practices in JavaScript to create published simulation found at
https://phet.colorado.edu/en/simulation/plinko-probability
– Developed open source simulation in conjunction with PHETsims University of Colorado Boulder
organization
– Worked directly with product code and source tree in development environment
– Ensured that codebase was well documented and ready for internal code review

positions.title: HelpDesk Technician
positions.description:
– Trained to solve hardware and software problems for PCs and Macintoshes as well as for printers, scanners, and other equipment. 
– Assisted campus of over 1600 students, faculty, and staff resolving diverse hardware and software problems
– Ensured quick resolution of user concerns and escalated more complicated support issues to senior
helpdesk technicians

honors.title: 3rd Place in Columbus State University Calculus Competition
honors.description: Open to Calculus students from Colleges and Universities in the region by invitation and AP Calculus students from Columbus area high schools.
honors.issuer: Issued by Columbus State University · Apr 2014

honors.title: Danforth Creative Efforts Award
honors.description: Danforth Creative Effort Prizes were awarded many years from gifts provided by Mr. William H. Danforth for creative ideals in some field of labor at Berea College.  In 1968, the Danforth Foundation provided an endowment of $7,500, the income from which is used for the Danforth Creative Effort Prizes.  The ideas must be original, tried in the program, and save more money than they cost.  These prizes honor students whose products of imagination and effort have importance and impact beyond the worker’s span of time at Berea.

projects.title: Data Hub
projects.description:
As a part of one of my courses, Embedded Systems, the class endeavored to design a sensor that would monitor temperature and humidity for Pine Mountain settlement school. We split the tasks of different components of the sensor. The task that I took on is a Flask application that receives, stores, and notifies users of data from the various temperature and
humidity sensors deployed at Pine Mountain Settlement School.  Pine Mountain has sensitive archives and animals that are in danger if the temperature are too low or too high. The application takes the readings from the sensor and displays it on a dashboard. If the temperature is out of an acceptable range administrator receive a text message warning them or the danger.

projects.description:
Sales and inventory tracking system that updates inventory based on sales order status
created for non-profit organization Grow Appalachia
